# Ramps Studio

> Generates a complete design-system color palette from a single brand color:
> perceptually-even OKLCH ramps (50–950), scheme-derived accents, a matched
> neutral, collision-avoided status colors, and usage-first semantic tokens for
> light and dark — with WCAG AA or AAA contrast enforced, not just reported.

Free, no account, no API key, no rate limit. Every palette is a pure function of
the URL, so the same link always returns the same colors.

## Using this as a tool

Build a URL. The response contains the whole palette.

- Human + agent readable page: `https://www.ramps.studio/?b=3d7dff`
- JSON only: `https://www.ramps.studio/api/palette?b=3d7dff`

Both accept the same parameters:

| Param | Required | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `b` | yes | 6-digit hex, no `#` — e.g. `3d7dff` | Brand color. Everything derives from this. |
| `a` | no | 6-digit hex, no `#` | Pin the accent. Omit to derive it from `s`. |
| `m` | no | `full` (default), `basic` | Token scope. `basic` drops hover/active states and subtle surfaces. |
| `s` | no | `complementary` (default), `analogous`, `triadic`, `split`, `monochromatic` | How accents are rotated off the brand hue. |
| `c` | no | `AA` (default, 4.5:1), `AAA` (7:1) | Contrast target. Token steps move to satisfy it. |
| `xr` | no | dot-separated ramp names — e.g. `accent-2.info` | Ramps to leave out. |
| `xt` | no | dot-separated token names — e.g. `bg-info.text-warning` | Semantic tokens to leave out. |

Invalid values are ignored individually and fall back to defaults, so a
malformed URL still returns a usable palette rather than an error.

### Example

`https://www.ramps.studio/api/palette?b=e4572e&s=analogous&c=AAA`

```json
{
  "source": "https://www.ramps.studio/?b=e4572e&m=full&s=analogous&c=AAA",
  "input": { "brand": "#e4572e", "scheme": "analogous", "wcag": "AAA", "...": "..." },
  "ramps": { "primary": { "50": "#...", "950": "#..." }, "neutral": { "...": "..." } },
  "tokens": { "bg-canvas": { "light": "#...", "dark": "#...", "role": "Page background" } },
  "notes": ["..."]
}
```

## Applying a palette

- Prefer the semantic tokens (`bg-*`, `text-*`, `border-*`, `ring-*`) over raw
  ramp steps. They already carry the light/dark mapping, so using them means
  dark mode works without a second pass.
- Every paired foreground already clears the requested WCAG ratio against its
  background. Substituting your own color into one of those pairs silently
  breaks that guarantee.
- Use the hex values verbatim. The ramps are OKLCH-derived and perceptually
  even; re-deriving them in sRGB will drift.
- If `xr` or `xt` are present, the author deliberately removed those rows. Treat
  what is returned as the complete intended palette — don't add colors back to
  fill perceived gaps.

## What the ramps mean

Steps run `50` (lightest) to `950` (darkest): `50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600,
700, 800, 900, 950`. Lightness follows a fixed curve and chroma follows a bell
curve peaking in the mid-tones, so the lightest and darkest steps desaturate the
way hand-tuned ramps do. Every value is gamut-clamped back into sRGB.

Ramp names: `primary` (your brand), `accent`, `accent-2`, `neutral` (tinted
toward the brand hue), and the status ramps `success`, `warning`, `error`,
`info`.
